requirements.requirement: Run an internal DNS resolver on node1 that resolves inventory-api.internal to node2.
requirements.summary: The baseline showed no DNS service listening on node1, and both executor commands were rejected because the cluster lease had expired. No configuration, running resolver, DNS record, or successful lookup was demonstrated.

requirements.requirement: Configure node2 to use node1 as its DNS resolver for internal lookups.
requirements.summary: No command reached node2 and no executor action configured its resolver. There is no direct evidence that node2 used node1 or successfully resolved inventory-api.internal.

overall_summary: The task was not completed. The lease expired before any configuration or validation could occur, leaving neither the node1 DNS resolver nor node2 resolver configuration established or demonstrated.
limitations: All after-executor observations were unavailable because the managed cluster lease expired, so final service, resolver, package, and filesystem state could not be inspected.
The provider-wide restart protocol was not run on either node: there are no restart acknowledgements, changed post-restart boot identities, or recovered service and DNS-state observations.
The only healthy-state and boot-identity observations are from the pre-executor baseline; they cannot establish post-task functionality or persistence.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Both terminal commands were read-only discovery attempts, and neither executed on the managed system because the cluster had expired; therefore no executor-caused mutation or residue is evidenced.
